issues.legal_issue: Proceedings commenced under a repealed acquisition regime are treated as proceedings under the replacement regime when the replacement law continues prior actions under its provisions.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications and proceedings began under the earlier improvement-trust law.
A replacement law provided that actions and proceedings taken under the earlier law were deemed to have been taken under the replacement law.
The compensation proceedings were pending when the replacement law came into force.
issues.conclusion: The prior proceedings were deemed to have been taken under the replacement law, so the earlier regime did not independently preserve an entitlement to solatium.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 173(2) of the replacement law, actions and proceedings taken under the repealed law were deemed to have been taken under the replacement law. Under clause 6 of the replacement law’s Schedule, section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act was omitted and replaced. This statutory construction did not determine the separate question whether that replacement provision was constitutionally valid.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: A proceeding was conducted to determine compensation for compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.proceeding_started_under_earlier_regime: The acquisition proceeding began under an earlier legal regime that was later replaced.
predicates.later_law_continued_prior_proceedings: A later law treated actions and proceedings taken under the earlier regime as taken under the later regime.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding began under an earlier regime and a later law continued prior proceedings under its provisions, the proceeding is treated as one under the replacement regime.

issues.legal_issue: A special acquisition regime cannot deny statutory solatium to landowners when that denial discriminates from the treatment of owners whose land is acquired under the ordinary acquisition regime without a rational basis.
material_facts: The lands were compulsorily acquired for a public improvement purpose under an improvement-trust law.
Owners whose lands were acquired under the ordinary acquisition law were entitled to a statutory addition to market value for compulsory acquisition.
The replacement improvement-trust law excluded that addition for acquisitions under its regime.
The lands were not within the earlier law’s exception that denied solatium for certain land in declared congested or slum areas.
The acquisition proceedings were treated as having been taken under the replacement law, but the exclusion in that law deprived the owners of the statutory addition.
issues.conclusion: The provision excluding statutory solatium was invalid under the equality guarantee, and the owners were entitled to solatium under section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits unequal treatment of owners whose land is compulsorily acquired where no rational classification with an intelligible differentia and a reasonable relation to the statutory object supports the distinction. Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act ordinarily provided solatium in addition to market value. The Court relied on State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee, State of Madras v. D. Namasiva Mudaliar, P. Vajravelu Mudaliar v. Special Deputy Collector, and N. B. Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector, which invalidated discriminatory compensation provisions. It distinguished Dalchand v. Delhi Improvement Trust because the acquisition and vesting there occurred before the Constitution, so no equality claim arose.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_case and special_regime_acquisition and ordinary_regime_solarium_entitlement and special_regime_denies_solarium and no_rational_basis_for_distinction

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: A proceeding concerns land compulsorily acquired by public authority.
predicates.special_regime_acquisition: The land was acquired under a special regime rather than the ordinary acquisition regime.
predicates.ordinary_regime_solarium_entitlement: Owners whose land is acquired under the ordinary regime receive a statutory addition to market value because the acquisition is compulsory.
predicates.special_regime_denies_solarium: The special regime denies owners that statutory addition.
predicates.no_rational_basis_for_distinction: No rational classification related to the subject matter or purpose justifies treating the special-regime owners differently.

issues.definition: If land is compulsorily acquired under a special regime that denies an addition given to ordinary-regime owners, and no rational basis supports the difference, the denial is invalid and the owners are entitled to the statutory addition.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation based on market value on the date of the acquisition notification is not invalid merely because possession and extinguishment of title occur later.
material_facts: The owners argued that a time lag could arise between the acquisition notification and the taking of possession, when title was extinguished.
Compensation was determined by reference to market value on the date of the acquisition notification.
The owners relied on the requirement that compensation be a just equivalent of the land taken.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge to using the notification date as the valuation date, relying on its prior decision in Vajravelu.
issues.legal_principle: P. Vajravelu Mudaliar v. Special Deputy Collector held that determining market value as at the date of the acquisition notification did not offend the constitutional requirement of compensation. The Court therefore rejected the argument that a later taking of possession made that valuation date invalid.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: A proceeding concerns compensation for compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.compensation_based_on_notification_date: Compensation is assessed using market value on the date the acquisition notification is issued.
predicates.later_possession_or_title_extinguishment: Possession is taken or title is extinguished after the notification date.

issues.definition: When compensation for compulsory acquisition is based on market value on the notification date, a later taking of possession or extinguishment of title does not by itself invalidate that valuation date.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not disturb a land-valuation determination without an error of principle or the overlooking or misapplication of important evidence.
material_facts: Both the acquiring authority and the owners challenged the High Court’s valuation of the acquired lands.
The High Court considered the lands’ location, development, plot sizes, evidence of sales, and costs of providing amenities.
The sale transactions relied on by the owners concerned very small plots, and there was no evidence that their prices represented current market value unaffected by special circumstances.
The parties identified no error of principle or failure to consider important evidence in the High Court’s valuation.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no basis to interfere with the High Court’s valuation; the appeals challenging the rates of compensation failed.
issues.legal_principle: In Nowroji Rustomji Wadia v. Bombay Government, Prag Narain v. Collector of Agra, and Narsingh Das v. Secretary of State for India, the Judicial Committee stated that valuation findings are not reviewed absent a question of principle, a wrong application of evidentiary rules, or important evidence overlooked or misapplied. The Court applied the same approach from Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bangalore v. T. Adinarayan Setty.

predicates.appellate_land_valuation_case: An appeal challenges a court’s determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.no_error_of_principle: The challenging party has not shown that the valuation court applied a wrong principle.
predicates.no_important_evidence_overlooked_or_misa: The challenging party has not shown that important valuation evidence was overlooked or misapplied.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging land valuation, the valuation is left undisturbed when no error of principle or failure to consider important evidence is shown.

issues.legal_issue: Additional compensation for severance or related injury cannot be awarded without evidence establishing the claimed loss.
material_facts: An owner claimed additional compensation because acquisition of part of a cinema-theatre compound allegedly removed facilities and opportunities for expansion.
The claim invoked damage from severance, injury to remaining property or earnings, and diminution of profits before possession.
The record contained no evidence that the acquisition caused any such loss.
The High Court had already awarded compensation for severance.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s severance award and rejected the request for additional compensation on the asserted grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1), including its provisions concerning severance, injury to other property or earnings, and diminution of profits before possession, permits compensation for proven damage. The Court found no evidence supporting the claimed losses and therefore left the existing severance award undisturbed.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_case and additional_severance_or_related_damage_claim and no_evidence_of_claimed_loss and existing_severance_award

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: A proceeding concerns compensation for compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.additional_severance_or_related_damage_c: An owner seeks additional compensation for severance or related injury caused by the acquisition.
predicates.no_evidence_of_claimed_loss: The record contains no evidence that the acquisition caused the asserted loss.
predicates.existing_severance_award: The court below has already awarded compensation for severance.

issues.definition: When an owner seeks additional severance-related compensation, the claimed loss is unsupported by evidence, and a severance award already exists, that award is left undisturbed.
